rationale: C16 is a strong concrete template: both proclamations respond to Korean civilian suffering, cite congressional authorization to designate a relief period, formally set aside that period, characterize aid as a tangible demonstration of American friendship and sympathy, and call for generous public support of private relief organizations. The later proclamation adapts the same machinery from a month-long clothing drive to a week-long fundraising appeal. C07 has a weaker parallel public-mobilization structure, while C23 merely shares period-designation and exhortation language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved on June 6, 1953, has requested the President ... to officially set aside the week beginning June 7, 1953
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Congress of the United States by joint Resolution ... has authorized the President to set aside a period of time for intensive effort to meet these appeals
shared_material.explanation: Both use a congressional resolution as the predicate for presidential designation of a concentrated Korean-relief period.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby officially proclaim the week of June 7-14, 1953, as "Aid to Korea Week"
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby set aside and proclaim the month of September, 1951, as a special period of intensive effort
shared_material.explanation: The central operative act is substantially the same, with the designated period and campaign name updated.

shared_material.child_excerpt: as a practical demonstration of our friendship and sympathy for the people of the Republic of Korea, I call upon ... our people ... to make generous contributions
shared_material.parent_excerpt: as an additional sincere and tangible gesture of American friendship and sympathy ... I call upon our citizens ... to respond promptly and bountifully
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared language links friendship and sympathy with an appeal for generous public participation in Korean relief.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to the end that the private relief agencies may be enabled to help more effectively ... the millions of injured, destitute, and homeless Koreans
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the appeals of American Relief for Korea, Incorporated, and its associated agencies, for clothing and kindred supplies for the people of Korea
shared_material.explanation: Both channel the appeal through private relief agencies serving Koreans harmed and displaced by the conflict.
